transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m here because no matter what anyone says, I know some people at work are secretly working together to set me up, and nobody seems to take that seriously. It's just incredibly frustrating that everyone else brushes it off like I'm making it up.

Have you noticed any other unusual experiences, like hearing voices, feeling controlled, or believing things that are clearly impossible, or is the main problem the belief that certain coworkers are plotting against you?

No, I definitely don't hear voices or feel controlled by anything like that; the only issue is this specific group of people at work trying to sabotage my inspections. Outside of this work situation, my life is completely normal—I get up on time, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends like I always have.
Is this belief limited to the coworkers at work, or do you also think people in other parts of your life are involved in the same plot?

No, it is strictly limited to work and only involves a few specific drivers and one of the outside maintenance guys. My family, friends, and everyone else in my personal life have absolutely nothing to do with this. Outside of my job, my relationships are completely fine and unaffected.
Has this belief been present for at least 3 months, or has it been going on for a shorter time?

Yes, it's been going on for much longer than three months, actually about a year now. It all started right after that senior driver publicly challenged me in front of everyone after the bus collision incident.
Has this belief stayed focused on the same coworkers and situation for the whole year, or has it spread to other people or other parts of your life?

No, it hasn't spread at all; it has stayed completely focused on those few drivers and that one maintenance guy for the whole year. Outside of work, my life is totally unaffected, and I still do my inspections by the book, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends. It is strictly a work issue with those specific people.
Has this belief caused any problems with your work performance or led you to avoid, miss, or change your job duties because of it?

Well, I still get to work on time and do my basic inspections by the book, but I have started avoiding certain routes and specific drivers when I organize trainings. It has also made staff meetings really tense, a few drivers avoid talking to me now, and my supervisor recently had to pull me aside because I get so worked up during safety report discussions.
Have you ever had any hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things others do not, or any other strange experiences like feeling controlled or having your thoughts taken over?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices, see things that aren't there, or feel like my thoughts are being controlled in any way. My mind is completely my own.
Before this started about a year ago, had you ever had a similar fixed belief or any other unusual beliefs that lasted for weeks or months?

No, I've never had any beliefs like this before last year. Everything was completely normal until that senior driver publicly challenged me, which is when I first realized they were targeting me. Before that, I never had any issues or felt like anyone was out to get me.
Have you ever had any other long-lasting unusual beliefs or suspicious ideas outside of this work situation, even if they seemed less intense or happened at a different time?

No, I’ve never had any other suspicious ideas or unusual beliefs outside of this situation at work. My life outside of my job is completely normal, and I just focus on paying my bills and hanging out with my brothers on the weekends. This sabotage at work is the absolute only issue I'm dealing with.
Has this belief caused you to avoid, miss, or change your work duties, or has it started affecting your relationships or daily life outside of work?

At work, it has caused some tension—I've had to avoid certain routes and drivers during training, and my supervisor recently pulled me aside because I get so worked up in staff meetings. But outside of my job, it hasn't affected my daily life or relationships at all. I still get up on time, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends just like always.
Do you believe this is part of a larger organized plot against you, or is it limited to this one work-related situation and these specific people only?

No, there is no larger plot; it is strictly limited to this one situation at work with those few drivers and the one outside maintenance guy. It has absolutely nothing to do with anyone outside of my job. My personal life, my family, and my day-to-day activities remain completely normal and unaffected.
Has this belief caused you to stop working, miss work often, or seriously interfere with other parts of your daily life outside of work?

No, it hasn't caused me to miss work or messed up my personal life; I still get up on time, do my inspections by the book, and hang out with my brothers on weekends. But it has definitely caused some tension at work, making staff meetings really awkward, causing a couple of drivers to avoid me, and getting me pulled aside by my supervisor because of how worked up I get over safety reports.

Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that seemed unusual or hard for others to understand, even if they were not related to work, such as being specially chosen, watched, or having a unique mission?

No, absolutely not. I've never felt like I was being watched, specially chosen, or had any kind of unique mission. My only concern is the sabotage happening at my job, and otherwise my thoughts and my life are completely normal.

Have you ever had any other fixed beliefs that seemed unusual or hard for other people to understand, such as being watched, specially chosen, or having a special mission, even if they were unrelated to work?

Like I said, no, I've never experienced anything like being watched or having a special mission. My life outside of work is completely normal, and my only concern is the very real conspiracy of these specific people trying to sabotage my inspections at my job.

Aside from this work-related belief, have you noticed any decline in your overall functioning, mood, or daily activities over the past year, such as trouble caring for yourself, social withdrawal, or problems at home?

No, my daily life outside of work is completely fine—I still get up on time, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends. However, the situation at work has caused some real friction, leading to tense staff meetings and my supervisor pulling me aside because I'm so focused on protecting myself. Some drivers even avoid me now because I have to be so careful about tracking what they are doing.

Has anyone close to you ever suggested that your belief might be related to stress, a misunderstanding, or another mental health problem, and if so, do you think there is any chance they could be right?

Some friends from my church have told me I'm taking work way too personally, and my boss keeps saying it's all just a coincidence, but there's no way they're right. They just don't see the inspection logs and evidence that I see every day. I am absolutely certain this is a real, coordinated effort by these specific people to set me up, not just stress or some misunderstanding.
Before this started, did you ever have any odd beliefs, suspiciousness, or unusual experiences that lasted for weeks or months, even if they were mild or unrelated to work?

No, I never had any suspicious thoughts or odd beliefs before all of this started. Everything in my life was completely normal, and I never experienced anything like this until the situation at work began last year.

Over the past year, have you had any periods of depression, elevated mood, or other major mood symptoms, or any other psychotic symptoms such as disorganized speech or odd behavior outside of this work-related belief?

No, I’ve never had any depression, high moods, disorganized speech, or odd behaviors like that. Outside of the situation at work, my life is completely normal—I still get up on time, pay my bills, do my inspections by the book, and hang out with my brothers on weekends just like I always have.
Over the past year, have you had any periods of depression, unusually high energy or elevated mood, hearing voices, or other strange experiences outside of this work-related belief?

No, I haven't experienced any depression, high energy, hearing voices, or anything strange like that. Outside of the very real issue of being targeted at work, my life is completely normal—I still get up on time, do my inspections by the book, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends just like I always have.

It is absolutely just a work-related problem involving those specific drivers and the maintenance guy trying to sabotage my inspections. Outside of work, my life is completely unaffected—I still pay my bills, handle my responsibilities, and hang out with my brothers on weekends just fine.

Outside of work, my life is completely normal—I still get up on time, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends like I always have. However, at work, it has caused some real tension, making staff meetings awkward and leading my supervisor to pull me aside because I get so worked up over safety reports. But my family, finances, and daily routines outside of the job are totally unaffected.

Yes, it has been going on continuously for about a year now, ever since that driver tried to show me up. It hasn't stopped or gone away at all during this time because they are constantly finding new ways to try and sabotage my work.

Have you had any noticeable decline in your overall functioning outside of work, such as trouble taking care of yourself, withdrawing from family or friends, or problems managing daily routines at home?

No, my life outside of work is completely normal and unaffected. I still get up on time, pay my bills, do my inspections by the book, and hang out with my brothers on weekends just like I always have. This whole issue is strictly limited to the sabotage happening at my job.

No, it is truly limited to just those specific drivers and the maintenance guy at my work. Outside of my job, my life is completely normal—I still pay my bills, hang out with my brothers, and go about my daily activities without feeling targeted by anyone else.
Do you believe these coworkers are the only people involved, or do you think there is a larger group or organization behind the sabotage that extends beyond your workplace?

No, there is absolutely no large organization or massive conspiracy behind this. It is strictly a small, targeted group of people at my workplace—specifically a few of the drivers and one outside maintenance guy—who are coordinating to sabotage my inspection work. My concern is purely about these specific individuals trying to ruin my career.
Do you believe these people are only trying to sabotage you at work, or do you think they are also influencing or spying on you in other parts of your life outside of work?

No, they are definitely only trying to sabotage me at my job. Outside of work, my life is completely normal—I still pay my bills, hang out with my brothers on weekends, and I don't feel like anyone is spying on me or following me home. It is strictly a workplace issue.

No, it hasn't caused me to miss work, quit, or disrupted my life outside of the job; I still pay my bills on time, do my inspections by the book, and hang out with my brothers on weekends. However, it has caused significant tension at work, leading to awkward staff meetings, some drivers avoiding me, and my supervisor pulling me aside about how worked up I get.

Like I've said, it is strictly limited to those few drivers and the outside maintenance guy at my job. There is no larger plot, and nobody in my personal life is involved in this at all. Outside of work, everything is completely normal—I still pay my bills and hang out with my brothers on weekends without any issues.
Did this belief start only after a clear stressful event or conflict at work, or did it come on without any obvious trigger?

Yes, it definitely started after a clear conflict about a year ago, right after a senior driver publicly challenged my authority and tried to show me up in front of everyone. This happened right around the time of a minor county bus collision that got media attention, which put a lot of eyes on our department. Ever since that confrontation, I'm certain they've been coordinating these "mistakes" to sabotage my inspections and get back at me.
Did this belief start only after that specific work conflict, and is it still limited to that one workplace situation without spreading to other areas of your life?

Yes, it absolutely started right after that senior driver publicly challenged me following the bus collision about a year ago. It is still strictly limited to that workplace situation; outside of my job, my life is completely normal, and I still get up on time, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends.
